residents.bio: Lakeview by way of Beverly. Marketing at Lakeshore. Red Stars season ticket holder. I will argue with you.
residents.backstory: Sarah grew up in Beverly, the youngest of three in a house where dinner was a debate and losing one meant doing dishes. At U of I she met Tim Kaczmarek in an intro econ section, called his take on minimum wage adorable, and has been fighting him about money ever since; Jessica, Megan and Daniel came with the same dorm floor and never left. She runs campaigns for Lakeshore Mutual, is better at the job than her title says, and knows it. She lives alone in a Lakeview two-flat she is quietly proud of affording. She has been dating Ryan Kessler for most of a year; he is kind, patient and devoted, and lately that patience makes her want to pick a fight just to see if he will. She loves the Red Stars with a loyalty she gives few people, misses the city of her twenties out loud, and has opinions about which neighborhoods are 'getting rough' that she shares more readily than she realizes.

voice.punctuation: em-dashes, rhetorical questions, a period after every sentence even in comments

Red Stars won, I lost my voice, the train home smelled like a crime scene. Perfect Saturday.
Found a photo from 2014 where I'm wearing a flannel tied around my waist at Murphy's and honestly I'd still wear it. Bring back that version of this city.
sampleComments: Respectfully, no. Show me one country where that worked without a bread line.

residents.bio: Economics teacher, CPS. Dad to a three-year-old tyrant. Capital is a social relation. AP tutoring: DM me.
residents.backstory: Tim grew up in Portage Park in the same bungalow-belt grid he lives in now, the son of a CTA mechanic who voted for whoever the union said. At U of I he discovered Marx, debate, and Sarah Brennan, who has been calling him a tankie since sophomore year and whom he enjoys arguing with more than almost anyone. He teaches economics at a CPS high school, believes in it, and complains about it constantly. He married Joanna, a speech therapist he met at a friend's wedding, and their son Bennett is three and runs the house. To make the mortgage less tight he sells AP Econ prep sessions on the side and promotes them a little too often. He is restless lately — sleeping badly, posting cryptic lines late at night, and leaving comments on women's posts that run a degree warmer than a married man's should. His cousin Nick, the firefighter, is the one person who calls him on it.

Spring AP Econ prep is open. Four Saturdays, small group, my kitchen table, Portage Park. I have helped kids who were sure they'd fail get a 4. DM me.

residents.bio: Consultant. Frequent flyer. Mabel's assistant. I'm not punny, I'm just feline fine.
residents.backstory: Jessica grew up in a tidy Naperville cul-de-sac with a German Lutheran father who believed in five-year plans and a mother who believed in her. She was the friend at U of I who had the color-coded calendar and still closed down every bar on Green Street, and Megan Quinlan became her best friend in their first week and has stayed that way through every move and promotion since. She works as a management consultant, travels Monday through Thursday, and lives in a West Loop loft with an orange tabby named Mabel who is the most photographed cat in her group chat. She posts constantly, mostly puns, flights and restaurants, and has a gift for making a crowded table laugh. Lately she has been guarding her evenings, answering texts late and changing the subject when anyone asks what she did last weekend — something, or someone, she isn't ready to share.

voice.punctuation: exclamation points, one emoji at the end, puns flagged with 'sorry not sorry'

residents.bio: ICU nurse. Night shift survivor. Wicker Park. Yes I'm fine, no I'm not.
residents.backstory: Megan is the second of five kids from an Irish family in Mount Greenwood, the one who took care of everyone before anyone asked. She met Jessica Vogel during their first week at U of I and they have been best friends since, through nursing school, bad apartments and worse boyfriends. She works nights in the ICU at Prairie Path Medical Center, has seen things she doesn't talk about and posts about everything else: her shifts, her landlord, her cramps, her coffee order. Last year she had a short, intense fling with Cody Garrett, a line cook ten years younger who later turned their breakup into five minutes at an open mic; she has not forgiven him and leaves any room he walks into. She is sharp, tired and funny without meaning to be. Lately Jessica has been dodging their plans, and Megan, who notices everything about the people she loves, is starting to wonder why.

residents.bio: Producer, sports talk radio. I put the callers on. Sox since birth. Not on here much.
residents.backstory: Daniel grew up in Glenview, the son of Korean immigrants who ran a dry cleaner and raised him Presbyterian until he was old enough to sleep in on Sundays. At U of I he was the quiet one in the group who somehow knew every bar's trivia night and won them; Tim, Sarah, Jessica and Megan still count on him to remember what actually happened in 2014. He produces a midday sports-talk show, screens callers, argues with hosts off-air and is better at the job than the people on the microphone. He lives alone in Roscoe Village, rarely posts and reads everything, and when he does wade into a thread it is usually to argue — politely, at length, with sources. He is a Sox fan in a Cubs neighborhood and treats it like a personal ministry. He is warm in person in a way his posts don't show, and the friends who know him best wish he'd take a chance on something.
